A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Denoising Neural Reranker for Recommender Systems, with complete main text and Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that all substantive content is identical.

before.justification: v4 reports original offline recommendation experiments in Section 4 and Appendix E, plus industrial online A/B results in Appendix E.6 and Table 11.

after.justification: v5 retains the original offline experiments, ablations, supplementary analyses, and industrial online A/B results reported in v4.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical noise generators, denoising and adversarial objectives, regularization, and training procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ML-1M, Kuaivideo, Book, and industrial video-feed evaluations, including all scenarios in Appendix E.

E2.justification: The comparator rows in Table 1 are identical. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the ablation, larger-backbone, retriever, diversity, and timing comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices D–E retain identical data splits, preprocessing, candidate counts, metrics, model configurations, training settings, and online traffic allocation.

E4.justification: The score-integration and objective ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity plots, noise-distribution analysis, and supplementary studies in Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: The Student t-test statement in Table 1, significance labels in Table 11, and reported DAU interval in Appendix E.6 are identical. No seed or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match. Examples include DNR-G's ML-1M NDCG@6 of 77.67 in Table 1 and the +1.089% realshow result in Table 11.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Equations (1)–(10), and derivations in Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about informative retriever scores, reranking as denoising, the adversarial framework, and empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: The interpretations of noise learning, retriever generalization, diversity, and online metric tradeoffs are identical. Appendix F retains the same limitations and future directions.

D1.justification: Implementation and preprocessing descriptions, Table 7 hyperparameters, timing information, and the code-release statement and URL are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier recommendation methods are identical.

P1.justification: The running title is replaced by 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026.' The arXiv stamp changes from v4 dated 1 Apr 2026 to v5 dated 17 May 2026. Body wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–15, Algorithm 1, captions, and placements are unchanged. The header and arXiv-stamp wording updates do not reorganize the page layout.

improvement.justification: v5 updates only the publication header and arXiv version/date stamp. The main text and appendices preserve the same methods, evidence, reasoning, limitations, and reproducibility information, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
